Charge traction batteries only in a designated, signed charging area away from racking, walkways and goods-in; provide eye wash, spill containment, PPE (face shield, gloves, apron) and chargers matched to the battery type

Ventilate the charging area so hydrogen released during charging stays below 1% by volume (25% of the lower explosive limit); use mechanical extraction where natural ventilation is not enough and keep ignition sources out of the zone

Separate the charging area from stored goods by at least 30 minutes fire-resisting construction or a clear exclusion zone of 3 metres; fit fire detection and suitable extinguishers; update the fire risk assessment (lithium-ion needs a thermal runaway plan)

Operators must complete basic training, specific job training and familiarisation, be formally authorised in writing and take refresher training about every 3 years; battery handlers need electrolyte and hydrogen hazard training
Update the workplace risk assessment and safe system of work for battery charging before the trucks go live
